summary: Steel fire tower in Jackson County, Indiana, erected in 1932 after a wooden plan was dropped; out of fire-detection use since the 1970s and kept as a public viewing site.

facts.design: Four-leg steel tower with a 7'x7' cab

access.note: Register calls it a popular public viewing site; Skyline Drive closes after the first snow until April 1

visit.trail_note: Drive up Skyline Drive. Climbability comes only from a hobbyist survey, not the state. Road closes after first snow until April 1; forest office 812-358-2160.

events.note: Steel tower arrived in September 1932 and erection began; the register gives a CCC build window of 1931 to 1935
Announced plan that a man would be kept in the tower fifteen hours a day; no later staffing record found
Register says not used for fire detection since the 1970s; decade only, no exact year given
Restoration completed, per the eastern lookouts history page

corrections.why: 27.4 m is 90 ft, the height given for the August 1932 wooden-tower plan. The register and the 1932 steel-tower reports give 80 ft, which is 24.4 m. A 1946 NGS description says about 108 ft; that conflict is noted, not resolved.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register credits the CCC with building it between 1931 and 1935. A hobbyist site quotes a survey page describing an earlier wooden tower and a later CCC steel one. The story reports both; the 1932 newspaper reports show the state's own forestry department erecting the steel tower.
Register and 1932 newspapers give 80 ft for the steel tower, so 24.4 m is used. The 1946 NGS description gives about 108 ft and is reported as an unresolved disagreement.

sources.title: Skyline - Indiana Fire Towers (by Mark A)

notes_for_editor: Record height 27.4 m (90 ft) is corrected to 24.4 m (80 ft) per the register and 1932 steel-tower reports, but the 1946 NGS description says about 108 ft, so the height is not settled. The builder is disputed: the register says CCC 1931-35, the hobbyist survey quotes a wooden tower first and a later CCC steel tower. The 1932 site is also described two ways: about 1.5 miles south of Brownstown (Sept 1932 article) and about 2.5 miles (NGS). The 2010 restoration line on the eastern lookouts page has no source of its own. The climbable claim rests only on a hobbyist site; the story does not encourage climbing. Staffing in 1932 was an announced plan, not a confirmed record. No notable fire tied to the tower was found in these sources. The 1970 staffed_last year is a placeholder for 'the 1970s'. Record access was 'unknown' and is now public, supported by the register and the DNR page. Search budget: one websearch.py call.
